request.description: Measure the compiled official MuJoCo model, nominal IK feasibility, contact behavior, and matched 10-substep action/braking responses before selecting a learning direction.

measurements.label: compiled physics and matched response baseline

request.rationale: The initial scientific distinction is whether the first goal gap should be attributed to learned control/hold behavior or to compiled inertia, solver/contact, or actuation semantics. Nominal geometry alone cannot resolve that distinction. This deterministic PI-owned measurement directly records compiled options and effective mass, analytic branch residuals and conditioning, joint-limit margins, contacts, and substep trajectories under saturated and zero actions from the singular start and valid IK branches. Outcomes that show contact or unexpected authority/solver behavior would redirect early work toward physical/semantic investigation; a contact-free nominal model with adequate bidirectional braking would support treating future failure as a policy/control capability problem and selecting training/evaluation accordingly.

measurements.label: compiled physics and matched response baseline

request.candidates_and_roles: No candidates exist. Working, best-known, and retained roles remain empty; M1 is a mechanics artifact, not a policy candidate.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed Python measurement (M1); no training steps, no policy candidates, and no evaluation panels.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate or development success evidence exists, so the gap to the 98% objective is currently unmeasured. M1 is a mechanics measurement and cannot establish episode success, hold robustness, or protected-evaluator performance.
request.current_synthesis: Observed in completed operation M1: the compiled official model has nq=nv=nu=2, timestep 0.002 s and 0.02 s per ten-substep control interval; the recorded mass matrix at q=0 is [[0.01210,0.000507],[0.000507,0.01019]], with explicit damping 0.5 and armature 0.01. The compiled options record zero gravity, Euler/integrator value 0, solver value 2, tolerance 1e-8, and 100 iterations. All 40 sampled radius/bearing/branch IK cases were joint-limit-valid, had FK residuals between 6.1e-18 and 1.4e-16 m, minimum joint-limit margin 0.215 rad across the cases, and Jacobian condition numbers from 1.33 to 5.29. No contacts were observed at those postures or in any of the 205 matched response cases, despite the link geoms being collision-enabled. In matched ten-substep saturated pulses from q=0 and valid IK branches, peak joint speeds reached 6.08 rad/s and peak recorded acceleration reached 791.9 rad/s^2; the full pulse-plus-opposite-action traces showed speed reductions up to 2.47 rad/s but not complete stopping within the following 20 ms. The q=0 zero-action case remained at its initial 0.08 m target distance over the measured phase. Interpretation: nominal point geometry, branch feasibility, and contact are not the leading explanations for the first campaign gap in the tested states. The measured dynamics instead make sampled-data braking, entry velocity, and feedback stabilization consequential for the hold criterion, so a policy/control capability investigation is the most credible next direction. These interpretations are limited to the deterministic cases and action protocol in M1: they do not establish learned performance, long-horizon passive behavior, hidden evaluator semantics, noise/delay, or the absence of contact outside the tested trajectories. Competing explanations that remain live are target/branch selection and policy instability during reach, insufficient braking at the 20 ms interface, and a protected continuous-hold implementation differing from the visible post-action check.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether a learned controller exposed to the official 0.06–0.20 m target distribution can both select a feasible branch and enter with sufficiently low velocity to sustain the complete uninterrupted hold, versus failing primarily during reach or stabilization. M1 makes compiled contact and nominal reachability less consequential in the tested region, but it does not test a policy or the official hold panel. A first candidate trained under a clearly recorded exposure and then measured with complete episode diagnostics would discriminate candidate capability from the remaining reach-versus-hold explanations. If failures cluster at entry or show high velocity and short held runs, control/stabilization development is indicated; if failures cluster by branch, bearing, or radius despite low entry velocity, the next work should target representation/branch-conditioned control; if research success is high but protected semantics disagree, evaluator interaction semantics become the frontier.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires a learned policy with at least 196 successes in the protected 200-episode official panel, where each success is a complete uninterrupted 2-second hold. M1 established the physical baseline needed to choose whether to develop such a policy or first challenge the compiled task mechanics.
request.next_direction_or_closure: At goal review, open the bounded capability inquiry stated in next_question and develop a first policy candidate with official-range exposure, followed by research evaluation using the hold and trajectory diagnostics needed to distinguish reach from stabilization. Do not redesign the compiled robot or infer goal progress from M1.
request.next_question: Can a first learned policy, trained with an exposure that covers the official 0.06–0.20 m target range, achieve the complete uninterrupted hold, and do its failures arise from reach/branch selection or from sampled-data stabilization?

request.closure_condition: Close this inquiry when a completed training artifact and at least one completed development evaluation provide a bounded answer about first-policy capability under official-range exposure and classify the dominant observed failure pattern as reach/branch selection, sampled-data stabilization, or unresolved/limited by evaluator semantics; a positive, negative, or inconclusive result is sufficient, provided the limits of the tested implementation and diagnostics are preserved for goal review.
request.goal_connection: The human goal requires a learned policy to achieve at least 196 successes in the protected 200-episode panel, with every success being a complete uninterrupted 2-second hold. This inquiry is the least speculative next step because no learned candidate exists and M1 cannot establish episode capability or protected-evaluator performance. A policy trained across the official radius range and evaluated with complete reach, entry-velocity, hold-run, interruption, branch, and saturation diagnostics can establish whether development should continue toward control stabilization or shift toward branch-conditioned representation and reach behavior.
request.question: Can a first learned policy, trained with an exposure that covers the official 0.06–0.20 m target range, achieve the complete uninterrupted hold, and do its failures arise from reach/branch selection or from sampled-data stabilization?
request.rationale: Goal review cannot justify official assessment because no best-known learned candidate exists, while another mechanics-only measurement would not close the immediate candidate-capability gap. It also measured peak speeds up to 6.08 rad/s and only partial speed reductions under an opposite action over the following 20 ms, so the inherited claim that the dynamics provide adequate braking is unsupported and is corrected here: sampled-data braking and entry velocity remain consequential alternatives to reach/branch failure. A first policy exposed to 0.06–0.20 m, followed by trajectory-level development evaluation, has high expected information toward the 98% objective at bounded cost because it both creates the first candidate and distinguishes whether failures occur before entry or during the uninterrupted hold. The method claim will remain limited to the implemented exposure, training recipe, runtime, and visible development evaluator; it will not be treated as official success.

request.rationale: I1 has no learned candidate, and the current recipe previously exposed only 0.14–0.20 m. This full-allocation run creates the first candidate capable of being measured against the official-range reach/branch versus sampled-data stabilization frontier; training proxies will nominate checkpoints but will not substitute for development evaluation.

request.description: Evaluate T1:checkpoint-120832 on the 160-episode non-overlapping research panel starting at seed 4200, recording complete episode outcomes and trajectory diagnostics for the reach/branch versus sampled-data stabilization distinction.

measurements.label: T1 terminal proxy-selected first-policy development panel

request.rationale: This checkpoint is selected from T1 because its official-range training exposure produced the highest recorded training success proxy (0.58) and reward at 120,832 steps, while the preceding 115,712-step checkpoint reached 0.54. The development panel is required to test complete uninterrupted holds rather than training proxies. The updated evaluator records target geometry, first/final analytic branch, first-entry step and joint velocity, longest hold and interruptions, final/minimum distance, speed, action saturation, and substep excursions. Outcomes with failures before entry or branch/radius clustering would favor reach/branch development; early entry followed by high speed, saturation, interruptions, or substep boundary excursions would favor sampled-data stabilization; disagreement between visible and protected semantics would remain unresolved because this is not the official evaluator.

measurements.label: T1 terminal proxy-selected first-policy development panel

request.reason: This is the only completed learned candidate and its development evaluation is the strongest current evidence: 150/160 visible complete-hold successes (93.75%). Its failure diagnostics classify 7 failures as no-entry reach/convergence failures and 3 as post-entry interruption/high-entry-velocity failures. It does not meet the human 98% objective or establish protected-panel performance, but it is currently the strongest evidence-backed candidate.

request.outcome: I1 is answered for the tested first-policy recipe and visible development evaluator: a fresh PPO policy trained with full 0.06–0.20 m target-radius exposure reached 150/160 complete uninterrupted holds (93.75%), below the 98% campaign objective. Failures were predominantly reach/convergence failures (7/10 never entered tolerance), with a secondary sampled-data stabilization pattern (3/10 entered but had high first-entry joint speed and repeated interruptions). All 153 entering episodes and all final states were classified on the open analytic branch, so branch coverage is limited and branch causality is unresolved. Substep excursions were recorded but cannot establish protected continuous semantics.
request.reason: The closure condition is met by completed training T1 and completed development evaluation M2 with radius/bearing, branch, first-entry step and velocity, hold-run, interruptions, final distance, speed, saturation, and substep diagnostics. The result redirects the next development decision toward reach/convergence and branch coverage first, while retaining sampled-data stabilization as a secondary mechanism. It is limited to T1's PPO recipe, seed, runtime, full-range training exposure, and visible 160-episode panel; it does not establish official 200-panel performance or protected evaluator semantics.
